title: Unawareness of data processing
description: The student may not be fully aware of how their submitted assignment data (including work file, student id, course, and timestamp) will be processed, stored, or shared by the Grades Portal.
assumptions: Student is submitting without reviewing privacy policy or terms.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on typical LINDDUN U tree for unawareness of collection/processing; no reference material available.

title: Detectability of submission activity
description: The data flow itself may allow detection of the student's assignment submission activity through metadata or traffic analysis, even if content is encrypted.
assumptions: Network observers or portal admins can monitor connections to the web app.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; typical for detectability threats in data flows per LINDDUN Pro.

title: Disclosure of personal data
description: The Grades Portal Web App may disclose or inadequately protect the received student data (work file with potential personal info, id, course, timestamp) during processing or storage.
assumptions: Portal has access to the data and might have vulnerabilities or poor access controls.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on disclosure threats in LINDDUN; confidence low without exact tree reference.

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Processing of student assignment submissions may not comply with regulations like FERPA or GDPR regarding consent, data minimization, or retention.
assumptions: Educational institution handling student data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a placeholder; typical for compliance threats at data recipient.

title: Disclosure of student personal data in transit
description: The data flow carries identifiable student data (student id, course, file reference, role) between processes; if the channel lacks encryption or protection, this enables disclosure of sensitive educational records to unauthorized parties.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on typical disclosure in transit trees

title: Identifiability of students via direct identifiers
description: Assignment & Grading Service receives explicit student id along with submission details, enabling direct identification of the data subject without additional measures like pseudonymization.

title: Unawareness of data sharing implications
description: The Grades Portal Web App shares detailed student and role information with the backend service without ensuring users (students or staff) are aware of or have consented to the specific processing and routing of their data.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness threat at source sharing act per LINDDUN Pro

title: Disclosure of assignment contents and student identity
description: Storing the assignment file together with student id, course and submission time in the Assignment Store risks unauthorized disclosure of personal academic work if access controls or encryption at rest are insufficient.

title: Detectability of submission metadata
description: The data flow itself may reveal that a particular student (via id) is submitting an assignment at a given time for a course, allowing observers of the network or logs to detect and link academic activity.

title: Unawareness of data storage details
description: Students may be unaware that their assignment files are being stored with identifiable metadata like submission time in the Assignment Store, leading to unawareness of potential secondary uses.

title: Identifiability of teacher via login
description: Teacher's authentication data in the request flow identifies them to the portal, potentially enabling tracking of their review activities.
assumptions: Login is required and uses identifiable credentials like username/password or SSO token.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on standard LINDDUN identifiability trees; no reference material provided.

title: Linkability of teacher to course submissions via metadata
description: Network or application metadata in the data flow (e.g., IP, session, request patterns) can link the teacher's identity to specific submission queues for their courses.
assumptions: Traffic is observable or logged without sufficient anonymization.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; threat depends on whether metadata is considered part of this flow.

title: Non-repudiation of access request
description: The Grades Portal Web App may log the teacher's request in a way that prevents them from denying they accessed or reviewed specific submission queues.
assumptions: Audit logs are maintained for compliance or security.

title: Disclosure via eavesdropping on data flow
description: Student names, work content and submission times could be disclosed if the web transmission from the Grades Portal to the Teacher is intercepted or logged by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the display happens over a network without perfect end-to-end encryption or that browser/server logs exist.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate as exact LINDDUN Pro tree not referenced; this fits disclosure during transit.

title: Teacher unawareness of privacy risks
